ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, registered agent appointees, and ultimate beneficial owners against the UN Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, EU restrictive measures, and the domestic list maintained by the Unidad de Analisis Financiero (UAF). Politically exposed persons (PEPs) trigger enhanced due diligence with senior management approval, source-of-wealth documentation, and ongoing transaction monitoring, in line with FATF Recommendations 10, 12 and 16 and the customer due diligence standards of Law 23 of 2015 and Executive Decree 363 of 2015.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Publico de Panama – Online Services Portal (https://www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be expressed in Latin script, with foreign-language trade names transliterated and submitted in Spanish-compatible phonetic form. The legal-form suffix 'Sociedad Anonima' or 'S.A.' must appear. Names must not be identical or confusingly similar to any name already registered, deposited, or reserved under the Ley General de Sociedades (Ley 201 de 2020) or prior Law 32 of 1927.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant or resident agent must file a 'Recurso de Reposicion' with the Registro Publico within 5 working days of the rejection notice under Ley 38 de 2001, attaching corrected alternative names. If denied, a 'Recurso de Apelacion' must be lodged with the Director General of the Registro Publico within 5 working days. Exhaustion of administrative remedies permits judicial review before the Sala Tercera Contencioso-Administrativa of the Corte Suprema de Justicia. The initial 30-day name reservation window is not extendable; a new deposit and fee apply after expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual statutory seat at the licensed resident agent's Panama City office is permissible for corporate administration, holding functions, and treasury management. However, ISIC 3250 / NAICS 339113 industrial manufacturing of sterile powder-free synthetic nitrile examination gloves requires a physically staffed, sanitary-registered production facility with operating licenses from the Ministry of Health (MINSA), municipal business licensing, zoning compliance, and customs/export registrations. A purely virtual operation cannot lawfully engage in the manufacturing activity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Statutory registered-agent office: less than 5% unannounced physical inspection risk. Manufacturing plant: approximately 95% likelihood of on-site inspection by MINSA health and sanitation inspectors during sanitary registration, pre-license verification, and post-license surveillance within the first 12 to 18 months of commercial operations.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley General de Sociedades (Law No. 32 of February 26, 1927, as amended), Title I — Constitution of Corporations (Arts. 2-9), Title II — Registered Capital and Shares (Arts. 20-60); subsidiary rules of the Registro Público de Panamá
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Mercantil (Public Registry of Panama, Mercantile Section)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública / Acta Constitutiva (Notarized Public Deed of Incorporation with annexed Articles of Incorporation/Estatutos)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a Sociedad Anónima. The authorized capital is commonly fixed at US$10,000 (B/.10,000) solely for registry fee calculation; shares may be subscribed but remain uncalled. The corporation must pay an annual franchise tax (tasa única) of B/.250.00 through its registered agent to maintain good standing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board ratifies and adopts the Escritura Pública of incorporation and annexed Articles of Incorporation as inscribed in the Public Registry of Panama. The Board accepts the subscription of 10,000 common shares of US$1.00 par value, representing the US$10,000.00 authorized capital, by the founding subscriber(s). The registered office is fixed at [address], Corregimiento de Bella Vista, Distrito de Panamá, and [Agent Firm] is confirmed as resident agent. [Name] is appointed President-CEO, [Name] Secretary, and [Name] Treasurer, serving until the next annual general meeting. The officers are authorized to complete the RUC registration, municipal Aviso de Operación, bank account opening, and all industrial, environmental and sanitary permitting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Clearance and Charter Drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Mercantil; document preparation by a licensed Panamanian attorney and registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Counsel performs a name and conflict-of-interest search against the Registry's online database. Upon clearance, the incorporation charter, registered agent acceptance letter, and subscribers' identity files are drafted and compiled. A formal name reservation is not mandatory; final availability is confirmed at presentation.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name containing 'Sociedad Anónima' and corporate purpose clauses
Passport copies of incorporating subscriber(s)
Beneficial ownership and AML/CFT identification statements
Registered agent appointment acceptance letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, an alternative name is selected and resubmitted; rejected name searches do not create a blocking record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Escritura Pública
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría autorizada (Notary Public authorized by the Supreme Court of Justice of Panama)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporating subscribers execute the Escritura Pública before a Panamanian notary. The notary authenticates signatures, applies notarial stamps, and issues protocolized testimonios required for Registry filing, RUC registration, and banking procedures.
required_dossiers: Draft Escritura Pública / Acta Constitutiva with annexed estatutos
Passports of all incorporating subscribers
Registered agent certificate of good standing
Payment receipt of notarial act fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Discrepancies in the deed are cured by executing an amended version or a notarial clarification (aclaración) before refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration in the Mercantile Section of the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized testimonio (protocolized copy), the solicitud de inscripción (registration request), and the official fee payment receipt to the Mercantile Section. The Registry examines the instrument, assigns the inscription number, generates the Ficha corporativa (electronic corporate profile), and issues the certificado de personería jurídica / corporate registration certificate.
required_dossiers: Protocolized notarial testimonio of the Escritura Pública
Solicitud de inscripción (registration request form)
Official registry filing fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, present the cured instrument or supplementary documentation within the Registry's stated cure term, pay any recalculated fee, and re-enter the filing queue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration (RUC) and Municipal Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; Municipalidad/Alcaldía of the operating District for the Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the incorporation certificate and officers' list to the DGI RUC online platform; obtain the RUC number and taxpayer certificate. Simultaneously lodge the municipal Aviso de Operación with the competent District treasury office declaring the industrial glove manufacturing activity, facility address, and projected volume, and pay the applicable municipal rate.
required_dossiers: Certificado de personería jurídica / Ficha mercantil
Notarized list of directors and officers
Registered agent verification letter
Lease or ownership proof of the operating address
Sworn statement of projected industrial operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify RUC inconsistencies by presenting the missing sworn statements or corporate documents to the DGI taxpayer service window; for municipal refusal, appeal within the District authority and obtain a provisional activity notice pending resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Rubrication of Corporate Books and Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) for ledger stamping; licensed Panamanian commercial bank supervised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the share ledger (libro de acciones), minutes book (libro de actas), and members/registros book to the DGI rubrication office for official stamping. Thereafter open the corporate operating account before the bank's compliance unit using the Escritura, RUC certificate, personería jurídica, and officer identification, enabling SWIFT LC and telegraphic wire payment rails.
required_dossiers: Ficha mercantil and certificado de personería jurídica
RUC certificate
Officers' and registered agent identification documents
Bank KYC and beneficial ownership declaration forms
Shareholder subscription list and proof of address of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI rejects book rubrication, correct missing stamps or fees and resubmit; if the bank compliance committee queries the file, supplement source-of-funds documentation and updated corporate excerpt, then resubmit for approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Annual Franchise Tax Enrollment and Post-Incorporation Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá / DGI, effected through the registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm with the registered agent the enrollment for the annual B/.250.00 franchise tax (tasa única), payable through the official payment portal under the agent's delegated authority. Advise DGI and the Public Registry of any subsequent change of officers, registered office, or corporate purpose, ensuring continuous good standing and eligibility for the industrial and environmental permits.
required_dossiers: Annual franchise tax declaration form (DGI-Registro Único)
Registered agent delegated authority letter
Updated officers' list and proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late payment surcharges are settled and a corrective declaration submitted; corporate good standing is reinstated once the payment receipt is recorded by the Registry and DGI.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) — Dirección General de Industria; Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) — Dirección Nacional de Farmacia y Drogas (DNFD) for medical device registration

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) — Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II — Moderate Impact: a simplified Environmental Impact Study (Estudio de Impacto Ambiental, EsIA) must be prepared and cleared by MiAMBIENTE before construction or operation, pursuant to Law No. 41 of 1998 (General Environment Law) and applicable EIA regulations, because continuous nitrile dipping lines generate process wastewater and curing emissions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with national effluent and receiving-water quality standards administered by MiAMBIENTE/MINSA (e.g., pH 6.0-9.0 and numeric limits for BOD5, COD, TSS, and residual latex) is mandatory for process wastewater; air emissions from ammonia and nitrile curing lines require abatement equipment (scrubbers or thermal oxidizers) with periodic emissions monitoring reports; off-spec gloves and nitrile trims are classified as non-hazardous industrial solid waste and must be managed under the national solid waste regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification (Dictamen de Protección Contra Incendios) from the Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá, including fire suppression, egress, and sprinkler compliance; structural load and building safety inspection by the municipal engineering department or MOP-approved licensed professional; occupational risk prevention and workplace health clearance through MITRADEL (Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral), including CSS employer registration and mandatory occupational health and safety programs.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas de Panamá; official e-services portal: SIRI (Sistema de Información de Registro de Ingresos), accessible at https://dgi.mef.gob.pa.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: To procure the statutory Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC) for a Panama Sociedad Anónima: (1) incorporate and register the S.A. in the Registro Público de Panamá through a licensed resident agent; (2) submit the DGI electronic pre-registration via SIRI attaching the public-registry certificate, corporate bylaws, resident-agent appointment, and registered-office proof; (3) obtain the permanent RUC and activate the ITBMS (VAT) and ISR (income tax) filing profiles; (4) complete the municipal Aviso de Operación and industrial-license formalities in the plant municipality; (5) procure a DGI-accredited electronic signature for mandatory digital filing. Foreign-incorporated entities must register a local branch (sucursal) in the Registro Público and appoint a resident legal representative before the DGI will activate the RUC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not recognize check-the-box, conduit, or hybrid-mismatch entity elections; the S.A. is inherently an entity-level taxpayer on a territorial (source-based) basis. Available statutory elections include: (i) the Alternative Method (Método Alterno) under Article 699-A of the Código Fiscal, computing ISR at 25% of deemed income equal to 11.7% of net taxable gross receipts when this exceeds the ordinary net-income result; (ii) application for free-zone/maquila and drawback export regimes that exempt inputs and capital goods from ITBMS; (iii) application for the Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime under Law 41 of 2007 for group back-office and logistics functions; and (iv) the election to evidence that dividends are paid from profits already subject to ISR, applying the 5% dividend withholding tax instead of the 10% rate on non-taxed territorial or exempt income.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS), the Panamanian VAT-equivalent indirect tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No corporate turnover threshold applies: every entity performing taxable supplies in Panama must obtain the RUC and register for ITBMS before commencing activities. A simplified small-taxpayer regime exists only for natural persons with annual gross receipts not exceeding PAB 36,000 (USD 36,000) and is not available to a Sociedad Anónima.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama enforces a mandatory electronic invoicing (Factura Electrónica) system. Taxpayers must issue invoices exclusively through the DGI web portal or DGI-certified private software integrated by API; each invoice is transmitted to the DGI in real time for fiscal clearance and receives a unique acceptance code and QR verification stamp. The software must validate the seller's RUC and ITBMS status prior to issuance. Paper invoices no longer support ITBMS credits on the buyer side, and non-compliant electronic emission triggers automatic digital audit flags and per-invoice monetary fines.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: ITBMS zero-rating applies to export sales of movable goods (including sterile examination nitrile gloves) only when: the seller is an active ITBMS registrant with a compliant e-invoicing system; the goods physically leave Panamanian customs territory under a validated export declaration; title passes to a non-resident buyer; the invoice is issued at the 0% rate with the export legend; and the buyer's payment in freely convertible foreign currency is credited to a Panamanian bank account. Additionally, the glove manufacturer must hold the medical-device sanitary registration issued by the Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) and any required export certificate to evidence lawful production for the overseas market.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación / Documento Único de Aduana, DUA) with port-exit validation
Bill of Lading (Conocimiento de Embarque) or Air Waybill issued to the non-resident buyer
Purchase order and international sale contract evidencing Incoterms (CIF/FOB)
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificación de Ingreso de Divisas) and bank statement showing the USD proceeds credited to a Panamanian account
MINSA medical-device sanitary registration and export certificate
Packing list and sanitary/fumigation certificate as applicable
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export transactions are a high-priority DGI audit segment. Failure to substantiate physical export or to repatriate foreign-exchange proceeds within the 180-day term causes the DGI to reclassify the sale as domestic, assess ITBMS at 7% on the gross invoice, and add statutory surcharges, monthly default interest, and fines of up to 200% of the tax assessed. The exporter may additionally be suspended from ITBMS zero-rating, disqualified from drawback and free-zone regimes, and exposed to customs-bond penalties. Fraudulent zero-rating declarations (false DUA, forged bills of lading, unrepatriated proceeds) constitute criminal tax evasion punishable by imprisonment of up to 8 years, joint and several liability of directors and the resident agent, and retrospective clawback of all claimed refunds and in-bond relief for the statutory limitation period (generally six years, extended in fraud cases).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Republic of Panama does not operate a central bank. The U.S. dollar is the official legal tender under the 1904 dollarization arrangement, and the Balboa exists only as token coinage at a fixed 1:1 parity. Banking and financial supervision is exercised by the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) under Banking Law 2 of 2008; the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) manages fiscal policy and public debt; the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) is the national AML/CFT financial intelligence unit.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current-account and capital-account convertibility prevail. Panama has no foreign exchange transfer restrictions, no currency exchange controls, no central-bank approval for inward or outward remittances, and no limitations on profit repatriation. A non-resident-controlled S.A. can freely receive equity injections, loan proceeds, or trade payments in USD, and can freely disburse funds abroad for raw materials, equipment, royalties, and profits. The only relevant national hurdle is fiscal, not monetary: profits distributed from Panama-source income are subject to a 10% dividend tax, while foreign-source income is not taxable if clearly isolated in the ledger and record books. Profit remittances to foreign shareholders are therefore restrained solely by standard corporate formality and tax compliance, not by convertibility.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export surrender regime exists. There is no statutory timeline for converting export proceeds into domestic currency, no mandatory percentage of export receipts to be sold to the central bank (Panama has no central bank), no obligation to route export billing through a local account, and no penalty for holding, investing, or disbursing export proceeds in any convertible currency. Exporters of synthetic nitrile examination gloves may invoice in USD, EUR, CNY, or any other freely accepted currency and may keep proceeds in demand deposit accounts at SBP-licensed banks without any liquidity or conversion requirement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Panama does not currently grant a standalone e-money institution (EMI) licence comparable to EU EMI directives. Banking Law 2 of 2008, later amendments, and the Panama Fintech Innovation Hub permit sandbox or limited-purpose licensing for innovative payment services, but such authorisations are subject to SBP supervision and generally require a local legal entity, a local compliance officer, and a minimum capital threshold. An offshore digital EMI or foreign electronic money institution cannot independently settle in Panama's ACH/CAM clearing and settlement system; it must either establish a supervised Panama branch or contract with an SBP-licensed bank as a sponsored settlement sponsor. For a manufacturing S.A. with material trade flows, reliance on an offshore EMI for primary cash management is not a viable fallback; a traditional commercial bank account should be established.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a non-resident-owned Sociedad Anónima, the SBP's Customer Due Diligence regulations require identification of directors, officers, shareholders, and ultimate beneficial owners. In practice, most tier-1 Panamanian commercial banks require an interview of at least one signatory and the UBO. Standard acceptance is a remote interview through encrypted videoconference if the following are previously notarised, legalised, and apostilled: incorporation certificate, registered agent certificate, Poder General (power of attorney), passport copies, utility bill proof of address, bank reference letters, and a current Directorate of Companies licence. Alternatively, the entity's registered agent or a foreign-licensed intermediary can attend a branch in Panama City on behalf of a director, but the final signatory must still complete an identity verification step. Directorship physical presence is therefore not an absolute statutory mandate for a low-risk medical PPE manufacturer, but banks may impose a branch interview at their risk appetite.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Stereotyped Panama S.A. without a manufacturing substance footprint, since medical PPE distributors are often shell-prone.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled constitutional certificate; current Registered Agent certificate and good standing certificate; notarised lease agreement for the dipping and finishing plant; active payroll register and social security (CSS) filing reports; metered water and electricity invoices in the corporate name; customs import declarations for latex/nitrile dipping machinery; purchase orders and supply contracts for glove powdering and chlorine-washing monomers; proof of factory insurance coverage.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity, nomination arrangements, or historical bearer-share suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified share ledger and UBO register updated under Law 23 of 2015 (amended by Law 70 of 2019); sworn statement that all shares are nominative or immobilised in a central depository; notarised disclosure of any trust/PIF where relevant; copy of the annual asiento (preliminary creditors' registration) and the tax return for the last fiscal year showing actual production revenue.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of initial capital injection inconsistent with industrial start-up profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original subscription agreement and bank subscription receipt; bank reference letters from capital providers; audited financial statements or reviewed interim statements; board resolution recording the capital increase; a source-of-funds narrative covering three years of personal/corporate income tax filings; investor passport, domestic identity card or corporate registry excerpt.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sterile examination gloves are a Class IIb/Class I medical device requiring sanitary and quality certification, triggering unlicensed-orientated scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Ministry of Health (MINSa) sanitary permit application or registered sanitary export license; ISO 13485 quality management system certificate in the pipeline; U.S. FDA establishment registration and 510(k)/import notification, where applicable; EU CE marking certificate from a notified body for nitrile powder-free gloves; sterilisation validation protocol from a certified Gamma or EtO contractor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant route for a non-resident parent or SPV injecting equity into the Panama S.A.: execute an SWIFT MT103 from the parent bank to the Panama USD current account at an SBP-licensed bank. The wire instruction must state 'Capital Contribution — Sociedad Anónima No. [PAN]', reference the specific subscription agreement and board resolution, and provide a clear opaque reference number for the receiving bank's AML screening. The receiving bank will file a currency transaction/AML report with UAF where applicable. Supporting documents kept on file must include the capital increase corporate resolution, subscribership certificate, investor KYC packs, and good-standing certificate. Because no central-bank report of foreign debt or equity exists, no prior approval is required; the bank compliance unit merely validates the source of funds. Inward remittances can also be routed as a shareholder loan under an SPV intercompany loan agreement, with a description 'Shareholder loan — intercompany funding' and an interest rate falling within the fiscal transfer-pricing safe harbour if any. For goods-import working capital, the inbound remittance code may reference 'advance payment for machinery / medium-term loan'; no national purpose code system exists, so the wire field and corporate back-up documentation are the controlling legal evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For an examination-glove manufacturer importing nitrile latex, synthetic rubber, powder-free coating chemicals, and packaging cartons, the primary clearing rails are: (i) SWIFT MT103 plain remittance for open-account supplier invoices up to USD 250,000 per transaction, using our correspondent bank at the seller's bank; (ii) irrevocable Commercial Documentary Letter of Credit (LC) for capital equipment purchases, especially glove dipping lines, chlorinators, mega-washers, and ethylene-oxide sterilizers; (iii) MT700 issuance by Banco General or Banistmo, followed by MT202 cover transfers; and (iv) for local costs such as rent, payroll, utilities, harbour dusting, and warehouse charges, ACH/Electronic Fund Transfer at Panama Clearinghouse (Cámara de Compensación) in USD. For exports, the manufacturer receives MT103 proceeds into the same USD current account; no documentation other than invoice, bill of lading, and certificate of analysis are needed to convert proceeds because proceeds are already USD. To mitigate processing bank delays, maintain correspondent relationships with the supplier's bank in the US, UAE, China, or Malaysia; use exact ISO currency codes (USD, EUR, CNY), invoiced amounts, and avoid 'no further description' free-form memos that trigger UAF query.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporation Franchise Tax (Impuesto Anual de Sociedades)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) - Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due annually on or before March 15 for the preceding calendar year; no grace period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory late surcharge and monthly interest; suspension of tax clearance certificate (Paz y Salvo); non-payment for consecutive years makes the S.A. administratively inactive in the DGI RUC system and subject to enforced collection proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta - Formulario 110)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) - Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed annually by March 15 for a calendar-year S.A.; if the S.A. has no reportable Panamanian-source income, a nil or zero return is still required for an active RUC.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines and interest calculated on the income tax due; absence of Paz y Salvo blocks share transfers, dividend distributions, contracts with Panamanian banks, and renewal of the municipal operating license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Municipal Operating Notice renewal (Aviso de Operación / Patente Municipal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Municipality (Alcaldía) of the district where the manufacturing or commercial establishment operates
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal due in the first quarter of each operating year, generally no later than March 31; not triggered for a purely offshore holding S.A. with no Panamanian place of business.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Municipal fine, possible suspension or closure of the establishment, and cancellation of the renewal certificate; the fee is determined by municipal tariff based on declared capital, premises, and activity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Registry confirmation (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Beneficial Ownership Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation in the March compliance cycle on or before March 15; any shareholding transfer or change in ultimate beneficial ownership must also be reported within 15 calendar days of the event.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines under Law 70 of 2020 and related regulations; non-compliant entities are denied tax certificates and good-standing documents, and registration filings before the Public Registry may be suspended.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No general statutory audit is imposed on every Panamanian S.A. Mandatory external audit applies to regulated sectors, including banks, insurers, and securities issuers, and may be required by DGI when the S.A. meets the high-wealth contributor threshold, when audited statements are needed for tax refund or credit purposes, or when the entity is part of a consolidated IFRS reporting group.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted in Panama for financial statements; IFRS for SMEs is available for non-publicly accountable S.A. entities and is accepted by DGI for local bookkeeping and tax reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each S.A. must keep a complete record of direct shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners in the DGI Beneficial Ownership Registry. A share transfer is only effective vis-à-vis third parties after delivery of the share certificate and entry of the transfer in the statutory share register; the resident agent must note the surrender and cancellation of the old certificate, and the new beneficial owner must be identified before the transfer is recorded. The annual confirmation must be made by the compliance deadline, and any shareholding transfer must be updated within 15 days after the event.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 - USD 1,500 per year for registered agent and registered office services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 - USD 8,000 for a full IFRS audit of a medium-size manufacturing S.A.; reduced review or compilation costs may apply when no statutory audit is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation exempts foreign-source income; Export Processing Zone (Law 41 of 2007) grants 75% to 100% exemption on manufacturing export sales; SEM (Multinational Headquarters) regime offers 0% income tax on global-service income; Colon Free Zone allows preferential effective rate of 2.5% on taxable income for qualified commercial activities; no municipal or local corporate income tax surcharges.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 201 (Declaración Anual de Renta, Sociedades No Forzosas) filed electronically through the T@-PA portal of the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) at tapa.dgi.gob.pa
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; monthly advance income tax prepayments (Form 101) are due on or before the 15th day of the following month
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year-end; for calendar-year taxpayers, the deadline is 31 March. A one-month extension can be granted upon prior written application to the DGI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net gross income from Panamanian-source sales of sterile examination nitrile gloves; exclude goods exported out of Panama when the exporter is registered under an Export Processing Zone regime.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation without a permanent establishment in Panama generally has no Panamanian filing obligation; a non-resident with a permanent establishment must report only Panama-source income in Box 1 and may allocate cost under Box 2.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales: purchase of synthetic nitrile latex, per-polymer compounds, dip-coating chemicals, stripping agents, packaging, and direct labor attributable to production.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a permanent establishment of a foreign entity, allocate historical cost verified by import invoices and customs entries; amounts paid to related offshore suppliers must be supported by a transfer pricing study.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Operating expenses: quality-control laboratory costs, electricity, high-speed dipping line maintenance, sterilization (ETO/gamma) fees, clinical-testing subcontracts, freight, and general administration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions must be strictly Panamanian-source commercial expenses; home-office general-and-administrative allocations are deductible only under an approved cost-sharing agreement and must be documented under transfer pricing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Rentas exentas: income exempt from corporate income tax, such as profits from export sales under Law 41/2007 within a qualified export processing zone, and foreign-source dividends received by the Panamanian corporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident permanent establishment may only claim treaty or territorial exemptions for income already taxed abroad; proof of foreign payment is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Depreciation of fixed assets: depreciable base and annual straight-line rates for high-speed dipping lines, curing ovens, leach tanks, glove formers, air handling systems, and auxiliary plant; standard annual rate is 10% for industrial equipment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Depreciation of import assets is allowable only when the asset is physically used in Panama; no Canadian/IFRS depreciation may be claimed without DGI concentration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base (renta gravable): total Box 1 revenue less Box 2, Box 3, and Box 5 deductions, adjusted for Box 4 exemptions and carryforward losses from prior years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The permanent establishment of a foreign enterprise must compute taxable income using separate accounts; head-office expenses are capped at actual reimbursement plus an arm's-length service margin.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax computed at 25%; subtract monthly prepayments and imputed tax credits (payments under Form 101). Balance due must be paid in US dollars (or Panamanian balboa at 1:1).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-owned permanent establishments are not eligible for the 2.5% alternative minimum tax regime relevant to distribution systems; the balance due must be remitted by wire to DGI's commercial bank clearing account.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: fine of USD 50.00 to USD 500.00 plus a monthly surcharge of 1% of the tax due for every month or fraction of month from the original due date, capped at 50% of the principal tax. Non-filing of a required return is a tax misdemeanor punishable by a fine of one hundred (100) to five thousand (5,000) balboas plus imprisonment of six months to two years if the delayed return is filed deliberately. Interest accrues at 10% per annum on overdue tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends distributed from net income already subject to 25% corporate income tax; 20% on any distribution of untaxed or exempted profits, including foreign-source income, if paid to a Panama-resident or non-resident shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident shareholder intending to apply treaty rates must (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the shareholders' country of residence; (2) submit that TRC and a Letter of Applicability to the DGI, attaching the entitlement form of the applicable double-taxation agreement (e.g., Spain, Netherlands, Mexico, Korea, France, United Arab Emirates); (3) file Form 201-D (Solicitud de Retiro de Dividendos) through T@-PA prior to the dividend distribution; (4) obtain DGI clearance before the paying company reduces the withholding tax. The paying agent must retain a copy of the approved evidence in its books.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 0% withholding on interest paid to outside Panama to financial institutions duly registered by the Superintendency of Banks; 10% on interest paid to other non-resident creditors. Royalties: 10% statutory rate for industrial patents, know-how, trademarks, copyrights, and similar intangible rights used within Panama; reduced to 5%–10% under many bilateral tax treaties; a 0% rate can apply if the IP is registered under Panama's Industrial Property Law and the use occurs wholly outside Panama.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Panamanian balboa (PAB/USD): mandatory Local File and Master File documentation is required when the taxpayer's gross revenue exceeds PAB 10,000,000.00 within the immediate prior tax period or when related-party transactions individually or in aggregate exceed PAB 200,000.00. A Country-by-Country Report (CbCR) threshold applies when consolidated group revenue reaches PAB 100,000,000.00.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama's Law 52 of 2016 and its implementing Decree 522-08-2019 impose economic substance requirements on Panama-seated entities engaged in 'relevant activities.' High-speed dipping production of synthetic nitrile gloves is a manufacturing relevant activity. The entity must prove physical premises, a meaningful number of full-time employees, operational expenditures proportional to income, and the conduct of core income-generating decisions within Panama. A compliant sterilization and glove production facility automatically satisfies these tests; failure to maintain payroll, utilities, or minimum operational data will trigger recharacterization, a 100% penalty on the tax privilege, and reinstatement of the 25% corporate income tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing a Form 201 that intentionally omits Panama-source sales of sterile gloves, or inflating cost of sales through circular EPZ-EU imports, or misclassifying intercompany royalty payments as duty-free technical assistance to erode the taxable base below the 25% effective rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine equal to one hundred percent (100%) of the evaded tax amount; criminal sanction of two to five years imprisonment under Law 70 of 2018; loss of all tax benefits and automatic closure of Export Processing Zone operating license.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, president, treasurer, and registered agents have joint and several personal liability for the tax debt; personal bank accounts may be attached; court-ordered travel aban, restriction from obtaining passports, and criminal imprisonment of responsible management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Dividend Withholding Failure – Repartos de Dividendos No Gravados
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Transferring cash dividends or shelf company credits to shareholders abroad without performing the 10% or 20% withholding and failing to remit the withheld sum to DGI on the fifteenth day of the month following distribution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Withheld amount plus monthly surcharge of 1% from date of distribution; administrative fine of 1% per month up to a total not exceeding 100% of the unpaid tax; if the distribution was made in bad faith, the law treats it as a tax evasion, triggering criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign the distribution resolution are deemed personally liable for the withheld tax and any late-pay surcharge; the DGI may pierce the corporate veil and attach personal real estate or vehicles; a protective order may bar unauthorized travel outside Panama.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the Panamanian manufacturing entity as a letterhead corporation without real plant employees, utility contracts, production equipment, or actual dipping operations, while sending large profit invoices to a sister company in Costa Rica or Colombia.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 52 of 2016, the DGI and the Superintendency of Non-Financial Entities may revoke the registration agent's license, impose a civil penalty of PAB 500,000.00 or 2% of gross revenue (whichever is less), and apply a retroactive tax at 25% on all exempt income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Corporate veil is lifted; directors and the resident agent face criminal fines of up to PAB 200,000.00; they are prohibited from acting as director of any entity in Panama for five years; travel bans are issued during the criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML – ML/TF Red Flag using Medical PPE Invoices
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using high-valued wire transfers from payment rails (SWIFT LC, TT Wire) to purchase sterile gloves at inflated prices from a related shell in Hong Kong, then laundering the surplus through a Panama Private Interest Foundation or offshore omnibus bank account.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties under the Panamanian Money Laundering Law (Law 23 of 2015): fine from PAB 1,000,000.00 up to twice the value of the laundered assets; criminal imprisonment from five to twelve years; freezing of commercial property, trade license suspension, and debarment from public medical procurement across Latin America.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, trust managers, and ultimate beneficial owners are subject to personal criminal liability; the court may impose a restraint order on personal assets and an international travel ban; if convicted, imprisonment carries a minimum of five years without conditional parole.
